newsitem.title: FRANCE: French central bank nominations split leaders.
newsitem.headline: French central bank nominations split leaders.

text.p: Parliamentary leaders are split over who to appoint to the Bank of France's monetary policy council, forcing the choice of two members of the key interest rate-setting body into extra time.
The mandates of journalist Jean Boissonnat and banker Bruno de Maulde expire on January 6. They were due to have been replaced or reappointed by the cabinet by the end of December.
But government sources said on Tuesday that the cabinet would have to decide in early January because the outgoing independent central bank's council had not yet given its opinion on the nominees.

Sources familiar with the process said National Assembly president Philippe Seguin, Senate president Rene Monory and Economic and Social Council (CES) head Jean Matteoli had failed to agree on a panel of nominees and would submit separate lists.

The sources said the main disagreement was between Monory, an ardent pro-European, and Seguin, who campaigned against the Maastricht treaty in a 1992 referendum and favours a softer franc and faster interest rate cuts.
Finance markets are watching nervously because of concern that the government might use the possible replacement of the two to try to soften the Bank's policy on interest rates.
A decision is not on the agenda of Wednesday's last cabinet meeting of the year and the next cabinet session is not due until January 3, just three days before the deadline.

"We are reaching the end of the procedure, but the Bank of France has to give its opinion (on the candidates) and to our knowledge, we have not yet received it," a government source said. "It will probably be at the very beginning of the year."
A member of the monetary policy council confirmed to reporters that the bank body had not yet discussed the issue.
The bank has been very cautious in lowering rates in order to keep the franc stable against other core currencies in the European exchange rate mechanism.

The sources said Seguin had put forward Robert Pelletier, formerly managing director of the association of credit establishments (Afec) and Alain Prate, a treasury offical and an ex-deputy governor of the central bank.
Matteoli put forward Pierre Guillen, former head of the CNPF employers federation and Jean-Rene Bernard, formerly head of regional bank CIC and deputy governor of Credit Foncier.
Monory proposed reappointing Boissonnat and replacing de Maulde with Pierre Achard, an aide to ex-premier Raymond Barre who is economic counsellor at the French embassy in Germany.
The sources said Boissonat had indicated he was willing to stay on if selected.
However, the sources said Seguin had in fact persuaded Matteoli to put foward Guillen, a well known opponent of the government's strong franc policy.
By law, the cabinet chooses two nominees either from a joint list of six names submitted by the three parties, or in case of disagreement, from three separate lists of two names each.
The government declined to comment on the nominees.

"We want interest rates to continue coming down and to ensure the Bank of France's monetary policy doesn't obstruct government policy. It doesn't at the moment," a source in the prime minister's office said.
